title.narrative: SC 1: Anticipatory action to mitigate reproductive health and GBV risks to vulnerable women and girls in advance of typhoon landfall in Catanduanes

description.narrative: UNFPA Philippines is implementing anticipatory action interventions in Regions 5 (Catanduanes) to address the impacts of STY Man-Yi (local name: Pepito) on vulnerable populations, particularly women. Key interventions include:SRH and GBV Service Continuum: The program activates coordination mechanisms to ensure seamless access to sexual and reproductive health (SRH) and gender-based violence (GBV) services prior the typhoon landfall and available during and after the typhoon struck. This includes the preposition of essential supplies, deployment of surge capacities, and mobile facilities to reach affected areas.Multi-purpose Cash Assistance: • Provision of cash assistance (Cash for Health) to pregnant women in their last trimester through their FSP following the local cash working group and WHO recommendation for 8 visits, targeted 2 visit for each women in 3rd trimester• Cash for Dignity kits• Cash for the Adolescent kits• Cash for Work/stipend to WFS facilitators and community mobilizersCommunity Cash Grants: Four Women-led organizations whose focus is on Health/SRH, Protection/GBV, DRR, entrepreneurship, or sustainable livelihood, with membership of at least 25 each, will receive a funding (2,000 USD each). By combining these interventions, UNFPA Philippines aims to strengthen the resilience of vulnerable women and their communities, enabling them to better cope with the challenges posed by typhoons. This comprehensive approach addresses both immediate needs and underlying vulnerabilities, promoting a more inclusive and equitable disaster response. UNFPA will work closely with LGUs, local implementing partners, and communities.
